what_worked: Power-law thesis is genuinely argued; growth-rate skepticism and 'graveyard vs leaderboard' framing show real analytical thinking.
fix_next: Verify every number against the actual dataset—zero-revenue count, total revenue, provider shares, and B2B medians are all wrong.
verdict: Strong narrative arc undermined by multiple fabricated or unverifiable statistics.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: '$270M+ combined revenue' vs actual $15.6M—off by ~17×. Slide 3: 111 zero-revenue listings vs actual 216 (and 11% vs actual 21.6%). Slide 5: B2B median $8,362 and B2C median $2,213 don't match reference on-sale medians or any obvious subset. Slide 6: Stripe 64% vs actual ~63.6% is close, but RevenueCat 19% vs actual ~18.9% is fine; however PayPal 8%, Paddle 4%, Gumroad 3% are unverifiable—reference lists only Stripe/RevenueCat/Dodo. Slide 8: '2.3× revenue' exit multiple is stated without specifying B2B vs B2C (reference: 2.35×/2.30× medians)—borderline acceptable but imprecise. Slide 2: average $133,750 implies total ~$133.75M for 1000, contradicting both the $270M claim and actual $15.6M total.

evidence.insight: Power-law framing (slide 2), vanity-metric debunking (slide 7), and marketplace-as-distress-signal (slide 8) are original, decision-useful angles that go beyond chart narration.
evidence.narrative: Clear thesis introduced on slide 1, built through distribution→zeros→saturation→B2B→infrastructure→vanity→exits→synthesis. Arc lands with a memorable closing line. Sequence is purposeful.
evidence.framing: N=1,000 and source cited on every slide, which is good. But no mention of substantial missingness (241 country, 288 audience_type, 274 category). No limitations. Audience never stated. The $270M headline is never reconciled and is wildly wrong.
evidence.accuracy: Total revenue fabricated by ~17×. Zero-revenue count understated by ~2×. Average revenue internally inconsistent with the headline total. B2B/B2C medians unverifiable against reference. Provider breakdown includes platforms not in reference data. Multiple core claims cannot be traced to the frozen dataset.
evidence.visual: Consistent monochrome palette, clean typography, effective callout boxes. AI-generated decorative images on slides 1, 3, 9 add no analytical value. Slide 8 scatter is confusing with sparse points and dual axes. Slide 5 dual-axis bar is hard to parse. Pie chart on slide 6 is acceptable.
evidence.ai_slop: Three AI-generated decorative images (server room, abandoned office, glowing map) are pure filler. Consulting-style punchlines ('The house always wins') are mildly inflated but the analytical substance behind them is real enough to avoid full slop classification.

change_reason: Removed 1-point bonus: the fabricated $270M total revenue (off by 17×) and multiple unverifiable statistics disqualify bonus-level work. Lowered framing by 0.5 for absent limitations and audience specification. All other scores confirmed as appropriate.
